# Devplane

> Devplane — the desktop workbench for spec-driven agentic development. Write the spec, dispatch any ACP agent, verify against your own gates, and keep the record of who decided what while you were not looking. One local-first Rust binary: no account, no cloud relay, loopback only.

The unit of work is a **change**: a branch, an isolated git worktree, the agent runs in it, the gate reports, the decisions taken, and a done certificate. A change may name a spec folder (Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro, or any folder `[spec] plans` declares) and the task lines sent to the agent.

**Verified** means: the latest run of the project's `[gates] check` passed, and the git tree digest it ran against equals the working tree's digest now (uncommitted and untracked non-ignored files included; re-derivable with `git add -A && git write-tree` in a copy). Named gates are evidence and never make a change verified. Touching any file makes a verified change stale.

**Devplane never approves a tool call.** It can refuse one (`never_auto`) or put one in front of a person (`always_ask`), in Claude Code's rule syntax. A `devplane.toml` or `~/.devplane/policy.toml` that will not load makes every gated call ask. An agent cannot answer its own permission. Every decision is logged with one of five authorities: `person`, `rule`, `timer`, `nobody`, `devplane`.

**Nothing auto-starts.** Hooks are `command` hooks that decide in their own process and write to the SQLite store (`~/.devplane/devplane.db`). The one long-lived process is the host — `devplane serve`, `devplane open` (hosts in the foreground if none is running), or `devplane app` (the host with a window). It publishes `~/.devplane/host.json` and is alive when `/healthz` answers. Read commands work with no host.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/quickstart/): see your sessions, connect an agent, open the workbench, start and verify a change.
- [Install](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/install/): installer, `npx devplane`, `cargo install`, the window, the Claude Code plugin, what lives in `~/.devplane/`.
- [The workbench](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/workbench/): the interface — palette, activity bar, a change's six views (Overview, Tasks, Review, Gates, Ledger, Agent), the review, the keys.
- [CLI reference](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/cli/): every command and flag.

## Commands

Every command takes `--json`. Starting, steering or stopping an agent needs the host.

See what is happening:

- `devplane ls` (alias `ps`): sessions in play and anything asking for a person, grouped by project. `--all`, `--project`, `--needs-you`.
- `devplane show <run>`: one run in detail.
- `devplane watch [run]`: follow events; given a driven run, print what its agent says (`--thinking`, `--history`).
- `devplane search <query>`: tool calls, questions and errors across every session.
- `devplane open`: the workbench in a browser.

What needs you, and what happened without you:

- `devplane inbox`: what needs a person, most urgent first. `--project`, `--needs-you`.
- `devplane asks`: everything an agent asked, and what became of each.
- `devplane answer <ask>`: `--allow`, `--deny`, `--option`, `--custom`, `--field`. `--allow` is refused inside an agent session.
- `devplane attention`: whether each inbox kind is worth reading. `--days`.
- `devplane audit [id]`: what was decided and on whose authority. `--without-me`, `--limit`, `--otel` (OpenTelemetry GenAI log records on stdout; nothing is sent).
- `devplane modes`: which live sessions decide without you, least-supervised first.
- `devplane issues`, `devplane prs`: open GitHub issues and pull requests across registered projects, via your own `gh`. `issues --ready` lists what a repository offers as work.
- `devplane snooze <id>`: hide a run's or change's inbox items; `--minutes 0` un-snoozes.

Start and steer work:

- `devplane change start "<title>"`: a worktree, an agent, and the gate when it finishes. `--project <name|path>` (repeatable: one prompt to several projects; every refusal reported before anything is created), `--agent`, `--spec <folder>`, `--task <REQ-3|file:line>` (repeatable), `--issue <n>`, `--no-worktree`.
- `devplane change list|show|verify|retry|resume|finish|offer|archive|export|review|prompt|stop|drift|adopt`: the rest of a change's life. Six computed states: drafted, isolated, in flight, verified, offered, archived. `review <id> [--by risk|intent]` leads with checks weakened or changed. `prompt <change|run> <text>` sends a message without stopping the run. `export` prints the done certificate (`--json`: an in-toto statement). `offer` pushes and opens the PR only with `[github] pull_request = true`, else prints the commands. `drift <id> --run <run> --tell|--accept`. `archive [--delete-branch] [--discard-uncommitted] [--force]`.
- `devplane report file|ls|show|start|reject|defer|fixed|open|discard`: findings one project files about another, delivered to that project's person; a GitHub draft is sent only by `report open`.
- `devplane attach <run>`: attach a terminal to a run, resuming its session.
- `devplane focus <run>`: raise the editor window that owns a run.
- `devplane gate run [--cwd] [--name]`: run `[gates] check` (or one named gate) and exit on the verdict: `verified` 0; `failed`, `no_gates`, `config_unreadable`, `unknown_gate` non-zero. Records nothing.
- `devplane rewind <run>`: files a run named for writing that Claude Code's `/rewind` will not restore.

Set up a project:

- `devplane connect claude|codex|copilot`, `devplane disconnect claude|codex|copilot`: install or remove hooks (and telemetry), diff shown first. `--yes`; `devplane connect --statusline claude` also wraps the status line.
- `devplane trust [path]`: allow agents to start in a repository after listing its hooks and MCP servers. `--dry-run`, `--yes`.
- `devplane check [path]`: does `devplane.toml` parse, does everything it names exist, is anything unsafe. Offline.
- `devplane explain <call>`: what the rules decide about one call, and why. `--tool`, `--input`, `--dir`, `--replay`.
- `devplane rules [rule]`: which registered repositories are missing a rule. `--ask`. Writes nothing.
- `devplane speckit install`: register the gate as a Spec Kit extension hook (`after_implement` by default). `--event`, `--dry-run`, `--anyway`.
- `devplane agents`: the agents Devplane can drive, including any in `~/.devplane/agents.toml`.
- `devplane doctor` (alias `diagnostics`): channel health, latency, whether a host answers.
- `devplane completions <bash|zsh|fish>`: a shell completion script.

The host:

- `devplane serve [--port]`: the host in the foreground (default port 47831, `DEVPLANE_PORT`). A second host is refused while one answers.
- `devplane quit`: quit the running host, saying first what that ends.
- `devplane app [--port]`: the host with a window (build with `cargo install devplane --features app`): tray count, notifications, one global shortcut, `devplane://` links. Nothing starts at login.

Run by machines, not listed by `--help`:

- `devplane mcp`: a read-only MCP server on stdio — `inbox`, `change`, `explain`, `audit`, `reports`.
- `devplane hook`, `devplane statusline`: the hook and status-line entry points `connect` installs.

Claude Code plugin (read-only; adds the MCP server and a skill, installs no hooks): `claude plugin marketplace add hupe1980/devplane`, then `/plugin install devplane@devplane`.

## Guides

- [Verified done](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/verified-done/): the gate, the tree digest, the six states, budgets, review, offer/finish/archive, the certificate.
- [Working to a specification](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/specs/): `--spec`, `--task`, ticked vs verified, spec drift, the Spec Kit hook and `devplane gate run`.
- [Watching sessions](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/observe/): roster, hooks, OpenTelemetry, status line; Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, OpenCode.
- [Driving agents](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/agents/): the built-in ACP agents and adding one in `agents.toml`.
- [The decision log](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/decisions/): the five authorities and what is recorded.
- [Reports between projects](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/reports/): findings routed to a project's person, and `[reports] deliver_from`.

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/configuration/): `devplane.toml` — `[project]`, `[workspace]`, `[gates]`, `[gates.named.*]`, `[policy]`, `[budget]` (`usd`, `max_turns`, `max_runtime`), `[transcripts]`, `[github]`, `[spec]`, `[questions]`, `[review]`, `[reports]` — plus `~/.devplane/policy.toml`, `app.toml` and the environment. Unknown keys are errors.
- [Permissions](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/permissions/): `never_auto`, `always_ask`, what a rule reaches, fail-closed loading.
- [Architecture](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/architecture/): the hook writes, the host folds, the API route table.
- [Security](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/security/): trust, loopback and the bearer token, what fails closed and the honest limits.
